research_page.title: FDA Clearance of Lumipulse pTau217/Aβ42 Blood Test
research_page.description: The FDA cleared the first blood-based diagnostic test for Alzheimer's disease, detecting amyloid pathology via plasma pTau217 and Aβ42 ratios.
research_page.takeaway_md: In May 2025, the FDA cleared the first blood test to aid in Alzheimer's disease diagnostics: the Fujirebio Lumipulse G pTau217/ß-Amyloid 1-42 Plasma Ratio. While highly accurate compared to PET and CSF benchmarks, it is not a standalone diagnostic and yields indeterminate results in roughly one-fifth of patients.
key_findings_md: Demonstrated 91.7% positive agreement and 97.3% negative agreement with PET or CSF amyloid tests in a 499-patient cohort (FDA press release).
Reduces reliance on costly PET scans and invasive lumbar punctures by detecting the presence of brain amyloid plaques via a routine blood draw (FDA press release).
research_page.methods_md: Retrospective multi-center clinical validation study analyzing 499 plasma samples from cognitively impaired adults aged 55 and older. Plasma ratio results were compared directly against established amyloid PET scans or CSF assays.
research_page.trial_evidence_md: The FDA clearance is supported by a retrospective pooled validation of 499 samples drawn from observational cohorts and clinical trials, including [POLARIS-AD](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05531526), [Bio-Hermes](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04733989), and [BioFINDER-2](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03174938). A peer-reviewed analysis of this dataset was [published in July 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42418465/), confirming a 91.8% positive predictive value and 19.6% indeterminate rate, effectively matching the FDA's reported figures.
research_page.sentiment_md: Public and patient response is highly hopeful regarding lower out-of-pocket costs and reduced invasiveness, though online caregiver communities express frustration over insurance coverage hurdles and the anxiety of indeterminate results. The scientific community views the clearance as a major milestone but warns against off-label use due to age-related biomarker confounders in amyloid-negative individuals.
caveats_md: Almost one in five patients (~20%) will receive an indeterminate result, requiring them to undergo traditional PET or CSF testing anyway.
Clearance is strictly for symptomatic adults aged 55 and older; it is not authorized for asymptomatic screening and must be interpreted alongside other clinical evaluations.
The summary data lacks demographic breakdowns, leaving it unclear if diagnostic accuracy holds across diverse populations and varying comorbidities.
relates_to_md: [Biomarkers](/research/biomarkers) — Details the broader clinical shift toward blood-based pTau and amyloid ratios in AD diagnostics.
[Amyloid hypothesis](/research/amyloid-hypothesis) — Contextualizes the underlying brain pathology this test is designed to detect.

notes_for_editor: The timeline event for this clearance ('2025-05 — First blood test cleared') already exists in the system, so no new timeline entry was generated to prevent duplication.

POLARIS-AD, Bio-Hermes, and BioFINDER-2 were kept as external clinicaltrials.gov links rather than generating new trial pages, as they merely provided context samples for the assay validation rather than being central to the document.
